In [[probability theory]], the '''matrix-exponential distribution''' is an [[absolutely continuous]] distribution with rational [[Laplace–Stieltjes transform]].<ref name="asmussen2006">{{Cite book | doi = 10.1002/0471667196.ess1092.pub2| chapter = Matrix-Exponential Distributions| title = Encyclopedia of Statistical Sciences| year = 2006| last1 = Asmussen | first1 = S. R. | last2 = o’Cinneide | first2 = C. A. | isbn = 0471667196}}</ref> They were introduced by [[David Cox (statistician)|David Cox]] in 1955 as '''distributions with rational Laplace–Stieltjes transforms'''.<ref name="bean2008">{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1080/15326340802232186| title = Characterization of Matrix-Exponential Distributions| journal = [[Stochastic Models]]| volume = 24| issue = 3| pages = 339| year = 2008| last1 = Bean | first1 = N. G. | last2 = Fackrell | first2 = M. | last3 = Taylor | first3 = P. }}</ref>

The [[probability density function]] is <math> f(x) = \mathbf{\alpha} e^{x\,T} \mathbf{s} \text{ for }x\ge 0 </math> (and 0 when ''x''&nbsp;<&nbsp;0), and the [[cumulative distribution function]] is <math>F(t) = 1 - \alpha e^{\textbf{A}t} \textbf{1}</math><ref>{{Cite web |title=Tools for Phase-Type Distributions (butools.ph) — butools 2.0 documentation |url=http://webspn.hit.bme.hu/~telek/tools/butools/doc/ph.html |access-date=2022-04-16 |website=webspn.hit.bme.hu}}</ref> where '''1''' is a vector of 1s and

: <math>
\begin{align}
\alpha & \in \mathbb R^{1\times n}, \\
T & \in \mathbb R^{n\times n}, \\
s & \in \mathbb R^{n\times 1}.
\end{align}
</math>

There are no restrictions on the parameters '''α''', '''T''', '''s''' other than that they correspond to a probability distribution.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1239/aap/1175266478| title = On matrix exponential distributions| journal = Advances in Applied Probability| volume = 39| pages = 271–292| year = 2007| last1 = He | first1 = Q. M. | last2 = Zhang | first2 = H. | publisher = [[Applied Probability Trust]]| doi-access = free}}</ref> There is no straightforward way to ascertain if a particular set of parameters form such a distribution.<ref name="bean2008" /> The dimension of the matrix '''T''' is the order of the matrix-exponential representation.<ref name="asmussen2006" />

The distribution is a generalisation of the [[phase-type distribution]].

==Moments==

If ''X'' has a matrix-exponential distribution then the ''k''th [[moment (mathematics)|moment]] is given by<ref name="bean2008" />

:<math>\operatorname E(X^k) = (-1)^{k+1}k! \mathbf{\alpha} T^{-(k+1)}\mathbf{s}.</math>

==Fitting==

Matrix exponential distributions can be fitted using [[maximum likelihood estimation]].<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1081/STM-200056227| title = Fitting with Matrix-Exponential Distributions| journal = [[Stochastic Models (journal)|Stochastic Models]]| volume = 21| issue = 2–3| pages = 377| year = 2005| last1 = Fackrell | first1 = M. }}</ref>

==Software==

*''[http://webspn.hit.bme.hu/~telek/tools/butools/butools.html BuTools]'' a [[MATLAB]] and [[Mathematica]] script for fitting matrix-exponential distributions to three specified moments.
